title: Cryptocurrency exchange, trading and payments
summary: LOC 2021 counted 9 absolute and 42 implicit bans. Lists below combine that report's examples (read via secondary summaries only) with unverified general knowledge; the EU, UK, USA, Japan, Singapore and UAE are licence regimes. US states add own money-transmitter licences. Laws change fast: verify each.

countries.name: China
countries.note: Absolute ban on crypto trading, exchange services and mining (PBoC 2021 notice).

countries.name: Algeria
countries.note: Named by LOC as banning all crypto activity; 2018 finance law forbids purchase, sale, use and holding.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.note: Named by LOC as banning crypto activity (Office des Changes). A draft law to regulate was reported; status unverified.

countries.name: Nepal
countries.note: Named by LOC; Nepal Rastra Bank declared crypto illegal in 2017.

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.note: Named by LOC as banning in 2018 (BCB resolution); reported lifted/relaxed 2024. from general knowledge, unverified. Current status uncertain.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.note: LOC listed as ban; State Bank bars banks from crypto, but the government moved toward a regulator (PVARA) in 2025. Status in flux.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.note: LOC listed as ban on use as payment; holding/trading in legal grey zone, pilot licensing regime reported 2025. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.note: Bangladesh Bank warns crypto use is illegal under foreign exchange law. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.note: Central bank law 194/2020 forbids crypto trading/promotion without CBE licence; religious opinion also negative.

countries.name: Iraq
countries.note: Central Bank of Iraq ban on crypto trading and dealing (implicit ban per LOC).

countries.name: Qatar
countries.note: Qatar Central Bank bars regulated firms from crypto; QFC tokenisation exceptions exist.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.note: No licensing; SAMA warns crypto is unregulated and banks may not deal in it. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.note: Mining and crypto trading restrictions; banks barred from crypto. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.note: Central bank/financial law bars crypto as payment; implicit ban per LOC.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.note: Crypto payments banned since 2021; trading allowed only via CMB-licensed platforms (Law 7518, 2024).

countries.name: Russia
countries.note: Crypto payments for goods/services banned; trading and exchange allowed under Digital Financial Assets law, mining regulated 2024; cross-border use via experimental regime. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.note: Decree 8 (2018) legalises crypto activity via HTP residents; Decree 367 (2023) licenses exchanges. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: India
countries.note: Not banned; 30% tax and 1% TDS, VASPs must register with FIU-IND under PMLA (2023). No licence regime.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.note: Crypto is a commodity, not payment; trading only via OJK/Bappebti registered exchanges. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: European Union
countries.note: MiCA regulation (EU 2023/1114) requires CASP authorisation. NOTE: EU is not an ISO country; applies to each member state - see per-state expansion needed.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.note: FCA registration under MLRs and financial promotions regime for cryptoassets.

countries.name: Japan
countries.note: Crypto asset exchange service providers must register with FSA under the Payment Services Act. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.note: MAS licence required under Payment Services Act and FSMA for DTSP.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.note: VARA licence in Dubai, ADGM FSRA in Abu Dhabi, SCA federally.

countries.name: United States
countries.note: Lawful but regulated: FinCEN MSB registration, state money-transmitter or BitLicense, SEC/CFTC rules. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.note: VASPs must register with FIU and use real-name bank accounts. from general knowledge, unverified.

countries.name: Iran
countries.note: Mining licensed, trading restricted, payments for imports allowed only via approved channels. from general knowledge, unverified.
